The last scene has the shape of the real failures: gear folded into how someone looks, beside a true trait in the same sentence, or told as a habit.

scenes.title: Brannoc takes the field
scenes.prose:
Brannoc came down to the ford at first light in the gold armour his grandfather had worn, every scale of it bright as a coin. He was the last son of the house of Avel, and the men on the far bank knew it from the armour before they knew his face.

He carried a spear of ash with a bronze point, and an old horn hung at his hip on a red cord.

"Who comes?" the sentry called.

"Brannoc of Avel," he said, "and I am thirty years old today, and tired of waiting."

scenes.title: Ielle at the market
scenes.prose:
Ielle had grey eyes, her mother's, and a way of looking past a trader's shoulder that made him lower his price.

She wore a blue cloak patched at the elbow and a pair of boots too big for her, stuffed at the toes with wool. In her left hand she held the purse with the last of the copper.

Tamsin Roe, her sister, waited at the well. Tamsin had been born in the winter of the flood and never let anyone forget it.

scenes.title: Heddick dresses for court
scenes.prose:
Heddick had served as steward to three dukes of Cardow, and he fastened the silver chain of office around his neck with hands that no longer shook at it.

Over his shirt went the steward's coat, green with a white lining, the one the duke had given him. He buckled on a short sword he had not drawn in ten years and picked up the iron keys to the lower gate.

scenes.title: From the wall
scenes.prose:
From the wall Ielle could see the whole line. Orrin was easy to find: his plume was black, and so was the beard under the cheek-guards of his helmet.

Beside him stood Varro with the wolf-pelt over his shoulders, the one you could pick out from a mile off. Kell, who had slept in his mail again and looked as if he liked it, was arguing with a horse.

Old Dace, broad as a door and older than any of them, wore the boar's-tusk helmet that marked him in every song about the war.
